description: Mass-battle Cannae gauge-band root-cause audit RATIFIED (merged via PR #73, ED-1094 merge-ratifies-by-default). Follow-up to ED-MB-0001's disclosed-not-chased finding that PER_CELL's combat mechanics collapse the H3-H6 Cannae-pattern historical gauge rows from a passing baseline to 0-13% losses against a 45-72% band. Produced by a Fable-led Workflow (4 parallel research agents; 4 independent adversarial diagnostic lenses -- clock_coupling, historical_fidelity, alternative_mechanism, design_options; each cross-critiqued by an independent Fable pass; Fable reconciliation re-verifying every contested fact against the working tree before adjudicating; a final Sonnet pass authoring the fix-plan document). RANKED ROOT CAUSE: demotes this session's own prior 'two racing clocks' hypothesis (test_envelop_reaches_rear_node's docstring) -- refuted as a general/gauge-scale account by gauge row C7 (a genuinely multi-subunit cavalry envelopment) passing its band, though it survives narrowly at the original diagnostic fixture's own scope. RC-1 (VERY HIGH confidence): three composition-coupling defects in the pool/morale accounting layer -- (a) a composed subunit's combat pool scales down per simultaneous-engagement pair while a single-subunit opponent rolls full pool into every pair (orchestration.py:504-528, POOL_VARIANT=C-ii); (b) two subunits' independent morale triggers double-erode one shared parent-Unit morale pool because build_army never populates a subunit's own morale field (hierarchy/units.py erode_morale/cohesion ~L404-431); (c) PER_CELL's casualty-fraction triggers use subunit-scale denominators (core/state.py:27-38). Plus two independent narrower bugs (a validator fixture ghost-cell construction-order bug, validators.py:205; a float-epsilon pool-floor bug, orchestration.py:527-528). RC-2 (HIGH confidence): the old PER_CELL=0 baseline that used to pass H3-H6 was itself an invincibility-bug artifact (multi-subunit cohesion structurally frozen at 1.0), not a working model to restore. RC-3 (MEDIUM, confounded): RC-1's couplings plausibly extend to gauge scale but this is not proven -- C4-vs-C7 (identical _envelop_army composition, one fails its band, one passes) is the sharpest unexplained datapoint. RC-4 (design gap, not a defect): the engine has no state between eroding and routed, so Hannibal's actual thin-and-yielding center tactic is currently inexpressible -- correctly deferred until RC-1 is fixed. RC-5 (LOW-MEDIUM, undiagnosed): 9 of 20 gauge rows fail for reasons unrelated to composition coupling at all -- flagged as a separate, not-yet-opened lane item. FIX PLAN (deliberately narrow, gate-free work only): 2 independent bug fixes safe to build now, 3 measurement/ablation steps (a per-coupling ablation harness; a gauge-scale frozen-wings ablation; a C4-vs-C7 mechanism trace) to close the remaining open questions -- explicitly does not build the accounting fix itself. DECISION GATES DG-3 and DG-4 RULED THE SAME DAY (recorded as an addendum in the audit doc, not re-litigated here): DG-3 = Option A, split the defender's pool symmetrically across pairs (Jordan's stated criterion: long-term integrity and fidelity to reality -- Option A reuses the existing pool-split mechanism symmetrically rather than inventing an underived engage-fraction formula (B) or a band-fit magnitude bump (C), and is the physically correct model besides). DG-4 = 'a blend of per-subunit as well as whole unit' morale (Jordan, verbatim) -- operationalized by wiring ALREADY-EXISTING, currently-inert machinery rather than authoring new state: hierarchy/units.py's agg_morale()/derive_rout() (~L1460-1481, troop-weighted aggregate for whole-unit rout) and cascade_morale_hit() (~L1482-1491, army-wide contagion) already implement the blend; the only gap is that build_army/build_envelopment/build_refused_flank never populate a subunit's own morale field at construction (confirmed by direct read, engine.py:243-246), so every subunit falls through to the shared parent pool. The fix is to default each subunit to its own real starting morale value at construction, closing the double-count by construction with zero new state. DG-1, DG-2, DG-5 remain OPEN, gated on the DG-3/DG-4 fix landing and the gauge being re-measured. Implementation of the fix plan + DG-3/DG-4 rulings NOT yet started as of this entry -- this ED records the audit's ratification and the two same-day gate rulings only.

description: Follow-up to ED-MB-0002: DG-3/DG-4 landed (PR #75) but did NOT close the H3-H6 Cannae-pattern gauge-band gap (draws unchanged). A fresh Fable-5-led adversarial audit of the shipped DG-3/DG-4 code found four concrete, reproducible engine defects surviving that fix, two introduced/made load-bearing by the DG-3 rewrite itself: D1, an outer troops_frac/army-size divisor applied to a subunit base_pool BEFORE pair_pool_contribution's own per-troop normalization, diluting a composed subunit's pool by its share of the WHOLE ARMY's troops rather than its own troop type/quality/density (orchestration.py, POOL_VARIANT=="C-ii"); D2, _envelop_goal's phase-1/phase-2 transition sharing one threshold for entry and exit with no hysteresis, producing a permanent limit cycle where a wheeling wing never actually reaches contact (hierarchy/units.py); D3, routed/broken atoms resurrected to combat pool 1 by an unconditional max(1,...) floor, contradicting SS A.12 "cannot fight back" (orchestration.py); D4, distribute_casualties tracking engaged columns as one union across a whole Unit, letting an uninvolved subunit (e.g. a far wing) absorb a different subunit's casualties by column coincidence (percell.py). Plus a harness-level force-ratio bug (gauge_mb.py's _envelop_army/_refused_army fielded 3x/2x a single-subunit opponent's troops, a silent side-effect of the LC-8 migration, making every DG-1 composition question untestable). JORDAN RULINGS (2026-07-05, via AskUserQuestion): DG-3 completion = "Intensive (per-troop, partition-invariant)" pool semantics -- the outer troops_frac multiplier removed entirely from the C-ii branch (pair_pool_contribution already normalizes per-troop internally). DG-1 = "symmetric at parity + majority pin cavalry wing so long as bottom-up emergent primitives approach" -- _envelop_army/_refused_army rebuilt at force parity (same total troops as their single-subunit opponent) via the continuous-scale troops/concentration path; infantry rows (H3/H5/H6) keep the symmetric center+2-wings shape at parity; cavalry rows (C4/C7) rebuilt as a majority (2/3) infantry pin + minority cavalry envelopment wings, matching the Polybius/Livy order of battle, via engine.build_envelopment unmodified. DG-2 (fighting-withdrawal/yield mechanic) = "create as workplan" -- NOT implemented this pass; captured as designs/proposals/mass_battle_fighting_withdrawal_v1.md, status PROPOSED. All four D1-D4 fixes + both ratified decisions implemented; an independent adversarial review found two of the six changes had real defects (D3's pool-zeroing was a no-op -- roll_pool/_sigma_net_boost both re-floor pool to a minimum of 1 internally regardless of the zeroed input, so the actual fix forces a_net/b_net to exactly 0 directly; gauge_mb.py's new wing_speed/speed kwargs never reached Unit.speed since Subunit has no speed field and it was never forwarded to build_envelopment/build_refused_flank) -- both fixed and re-verified. All 4 bat.py digest modes re-recorded (this touches shared, non-gated combat-resolution code, as ED-MB-0002's own fix did). tests/valoria 88 passed/16 skipped(numpy,unrelated)/1 xfailed. HONEST RESULT: draws are now GONE across H3/H4/H5/H6/C4 (were 100%/90%/100%/100%/66.7%), a genuine and dramatic change -- but these rows now OVERSHOOT their historical bands decisively in the attacker's favor (WIN-OUT) instead of landing inside them, except C7 which lands cleanly at the top of its wide band. Full 20-row gauge aggregate moved only marginally (4/20 -> 5/20 passing, multi mode n=30 -- H1,C1,C2,C6,C7; C1 newly passes). A controlled, isolated experiment (co-located vs spatially-separated equal-troop subunit splits, both vs an identical single-subunit opponent) suggests why: subunit_combat_pool's Command-driven combat score is not scaled by a subunit's own share of army-wide troops, so multiple spatially-separated attacking fronts against one defender can each roll close to a full, independent combat score simultaneously, tempered only by a small ENCIRCLEMENT_PENALTY tax that in this configuration falls on the defender, not the attacker. Whether this is a genuine partition-invariance defect needing its own fix, or the historically-correct emergent mechanism for why real encirclements are so devastating (with the bands themselves needing reconsideration), is explicitly NOT decided here -- flagged as a new, unresolved architecture question requiring its own dedicated Jordan ruling, not a silent magnitude tweak. RC-5's 9 unrelated single-subunit rows remain a separate, not-yet-opened lane item; DG-5 (racing-clocks) is corrected/re-confirmed closed (the original ablation's null result was itself confounded by the now-fixed D2 bug, not evidence of a genuinely settled non-race).

description: Jordan direct instruction (verbatim): "Please consider abandoning combat pools being related to the commander, and instead being solely derived from the subunit troop type, quality and numbers." Follow-up clarification: "And I guess subunit power is the aggregate or derivation of cell power." SUPERSEDES ED-899's Command-only combat-pool base (designs/provincial/mass_battle_v30.md SS A.1/A.4) -- Command remains live for morale, formation-hold speed, order-issuing, and derive_rout's Command-0 condition, just not the dice pool. New POOL_QUALITY_MODEL toggle (config.py, default ON): base pool = eff_power x eff_size x POOL_QUALITY_SCALE. eff_power is the troop-TYPE quality stat (TROOP_TYPE_STATS/SS B.2 -- levy=1 through knights_templar=5; SS A.1 itself already names Power as "determines dice rolled"). eff_size is NUMBERS (current troops / BLOCK_SIZE, continuously degrading with casualties -- no separate cohesion multiplier needed since eff_size itself is the smoothly-shrinking quantity). POOL_QUALITY_SCALE=0.5 [CALIBRATED] renormalizes the product to reproduce the historical T3-infantry baseline magnitude (~8, matching the old command=4/full-cohesion baseline) so pen/stam_pen's existing unscaled discipline/stamina penalties keep roughly their historical relative weight. Per Jordan's cell-power follow-up: eff_power x eff_size is already exactly the cell-level aggregate whenever a subunit's cells share one troop type (true today -- no per-cell troop_type exists yet, same gap pair_pool_contribution's own docstring already names); documented as such rather than adding a redundant per-cell loop here, since pair_pool_contribution/_pair_engaged_troops already do the real per-cell troop-density redistribution for pair-scoped resolution and will pick up true per-cell power the moment that data exists. Applied consistently to BOTH core/exchange.py:subunit_combat_pool (the live per-pair combat resolution) and hierarchy/units.py:Unit.base_combat_pool (the pursuit/rout path), which had been missed by a naive edit and would have left an inconsistency between main combat and pursuit mechanics. COMMAND_SIGMA_ENABLED's two prior branches remain live and selectable via POOL_QUALITY_MODEL=0, per this repo's standing ablation-toggle discipline -- not deleted, superseded-as-default. VERIFICATION: all 4 bat.py digests re-recorded (shared, non-gated combat-resolution code, same discipline as every prior pool-formula landing in this lane). tests/valoria: 121 passed/57 skipped/1 xpassed/7 failed (6 pre-existing test_names.py failures, unrelated; 1 expected digest-drift failure now fixed by the re-record). New xpass: test_envelop_reaches_rear_node unexpectedly passed once under the new model (not re-verified across seeds, xfail marker left in place per honest-disclosure discipline, not claimed as a reliable fix). HONEST GAUGE RESULT (multi, n=60): 6/20 -> 7/20 pass. Newly passing: C4 (cavalry envelopment, was WIN-OUT, now 83.3% inside 75-95 band), C5 (shaken-line exploit, now 95% inside 65-98). Newly failing/flipped: H4, the actual Cannae matchup, flips from attacker WIN-OUT (96.6%) to attacker LOSING badly (1.7% A / 65% B / 33.3% draws) -- a genuine, disclosed trade-off: single-large-subunit cavalry rows correctly reward raw numbers now, but composed-army rows lose because their PER-ATOM troop counts are individually smaller than the single consolidated defender's, an emergent property of the new formula, not a bug. OPEN, DISCLOSED RESIDUAL: lanchester_signature.py's strict trajectory-fit law-exponent check (melee should conserve p<=1.4, the linear law) fails under BOTH models. The PRE-EXISTING Command-driven baseline (POOL_QUALITY_MODEL=0, i.e. what was already in production before this session) already measures p~1.55 there -- a previously-undetected gap, confirmed unrelated to this change via git-stash bisection against the pre-session commit. That same baseline's simpler win-rate check also showed a 2:1 melee army losing 97% of the time; a quick trace suggests this specific check's methodology (a single 18-tick run_battle call, which mostly ends in a draw at this troop ratio) may be measuring decisive-outcome sampling noise rather than a structural defect -- flagged, NOT independently confirmed either way, left for whoever next touches this test. Under the new model, the simpler win-rate check now correctly PASSES (100% big-army win, +53.7 casualty differential -- the qualitative "bigger army should win" property is restored) but the stricter exponent check gets WORSE, not better (p~2.50). Tested extensively before accepting this residual: a sqrt(eff_size) variant barely moved it (p~2.35); a uniform pool-magnitude scale swept across {1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.0625, 0.03} plateaus at p~1.65-1.7 below ~0.15 and never reaches <=1.4 at any point tested. Confirmed NOT a Lanchester double-count: disabling LANCHESTER_ENABLED entirely leaves the exponent completely unchanged at p=2.5. Root cause (measured, not just theorized): the amplification is internal to the pool -> net-successes -> compute_degree tier -> DAMAGE_BY_DEGREE pipeline -- larger absolute pools have proportionally lower variance, so which discrete degree tier (Partial/Success/Overwhelming) each side lands in becomes near-deterministic from the pool ratio alone, and that discrete tier assignment compounds the ratio rather than passing it through linearly. NOT silently patched with an arbitrary scale constant chosen to look closer to the target -- a uniform scale provably cannot fix a ratio-sensitive test, since it does not change the win/loss ratio, only the absolute magnitude. Flagged as a genuine, not-yet-closed follow-up in designs/provincial/mass_battle_v30.md's own SS A.1 note and here: fixing it for real likely needs compute_degree's threshold logic or the DAMAGE_BY_DEGREE/Lanchester-coefficient calibration revisited, not another pool-formula tweak. description: DG-10 (opened by ED-MB-0007) resolved: the field/node movement path froze every sub-Discipline-5 body. _node_advance (the path FIELD_MOVEMENT=1 routes to since ED-1089) computed the per-tick advance as step = max(0, math.floor(base*disc_mult) + stance_mod); with the universal base cell-speed 1 and disc_mult 0.7 (disc 3-4) / 0.4 (disc<3), floor(1*0.7)=0 -> a balanced disc<5 formation never advanced to contact, making every such battle a vacuous 0-casualty draw. Per the mass_battle_v30 B.2 troop table this is the COMMON case: levy/light_infantry/heavy_infantry/archers/crossbow/sling/artillery are all disc<5; only cavalry(5)/knights_templar(6) cleared the floor (aggressive stance +1 or cavalry x2 the only other escapes). The continuous-velocity accumulator meant to prevent this (units.py head comment 'advances at its TRUE average rate instead of flooring to 0') was wired only into the LEGACY grid method advance_cells and sat dead there, never reaching _node_advance. Jordan ruled in-session ('fields, not grids. no grids.' / 'if it's broken and not commensurate with system, disable' / 'what even is the point of the continuous velocity accumulator?'): the math.floor is the grid-snap the coordinate field exists to remove, and the accumulator is itself only a Bresenham workaround for integer positions. Fix: on the FIELD path step is now the real velocity (no floor, no accumulator) -- _node_pos/_node_anchor are already floats and the sole consumer moves the anchor by eff=min(step,mag) along a unit vector; a disc4 body advances 0.7 cells/tick. Whole-number velocities are kept int so disc>=5 rows stay byte-exact; only genuinely fractional (disc<5) velocities become float. The legacy GRID path (FIELD_MOVEMENT=0) keeps its integer floor untouched -> the CI byte-exact grid oracle (test_mass_battle_byte_exact.py, pins FIELD_MOVEMENT=0) still passes. Field gauge goldens (bat.py cell_field/unit_field, NOT CI-checked): mirror/ranged (Line-vs-Line) stay byte-identical; the 8 decisive rows change because a unit that degrades below disc-5 MID-BATTLE (combat/charge shock) used to freeze in place and now keeps moving at its true reduced rate (confirmed by trace: wedge seed 0, side B -> disc 3) -- goldens re-recorded. NOTE: this fixes MOVEMENT only; it shifts the 20-row Cannae balance gauge (frozen units now fight) which is the DG-6-gated calibration surface -- NOT a balance-calibration claim, no balance constant tuned. The SAME grid-floor freeze exists in the WIRED engine (systems/mass_battle/sim/units.py:advance_cells, the one resolve_mass_battle/faction_action call) and is disabled there too (Jordan: 'subunits aren't moving when they have previously' / 'if it's broken and not commensurate with system, disable'); that engine holds integer cell positions (contact = set-membership on int coords) so it can't carry a true sub-cell field velocity (unreconciled with the field engine, ED-IN-0074 D5) -- the fix CLAMPS to the grid's minimum quantum (advancing body takes >=1 whole cell instead of a frozen zero) rather than carrying a faithful sub-cell velocity -- disclosed cost (adversarial pass): this flattens the sub-disc-5 speed gradient (disc 1/2/3/4 all move 1 cell/tick here, vs the field engine's 0.4/0.4/0.7/0.7); representing the gradient on this integer-contact grid would need the rejected accumulator or float positions, so the field engine stays the faithful one and this is an unfreeze stopgap. Discipline>=5 (incl. the wired resolve_mass_battle default of 5) is byte-identical (round(1.0)==floor(1.0); an adversarial A/B incl. mid-battle degradation and volley-under-approach found no disc>=5 outcome that differs -- degradation lags contact when movement is moot). description: Spatial-model v2 Stage B+C (the CIRCLE->OBB contact + collision upgrade on the FIELD path, per audit/2026-07-22-mass-battle-stress-test/spatial_model_v2_plan.md, Jordan-directed 'Euclidean motion, boxed footprint'). TWO parts. (1) ANALYTIC swept-SAT time-of-impact: the parked Stage B+C prototype used a per-cell-pair scan+bisection on obb_front_reach_overlap (~200k list-allocating SAT calls/battle, field path ~20-60x slower, stalled the producing agent). Replaced with a closed-form _swept_first_overlap_s (hierarchy/units.py): over one tick box axes+corner-offsets are constant (Euclidean motion translates only the centre), so each SAT axis is a linear-in-s overlap band -> an s-interval; intersect the <=4 axes' intervals, first-touch = left edge. O(4)/pair, zero iteration, ~15us/pair. Verified against the reference scan+bisection to ~1e-15 over 700 seeded fuzzed pairs (281 genuine touches, 0 mismatches). (2) COLLIDE-not-decelerate model CORRECTION (Jordan in-session: 'why are we decelerating to halt instead of just colliding at whatever speed?' / 'and wouldn't that break charging?'). The plan (and the parked prototype) made the TOI HALT surface EQUAL the contact surface -- both the reach-extended box. That DEADLOCKS: resolve_toi_and_commit parks a closing cell EXACTLY on the obb_front_reach_overlap *touch* boundary, where the strict-overlap contact predicate returns False, so contact never fires -> a permanent 0-casualty standoff at gap 2*(CELL_RADIUS+reach) (reproduced: head-on Line-vs-Line froze at gap 1.5 for the entire battle; clean main reaches contact). Root cause: reach was being treated as a wall to decelerate against rather than a weapon envelope reaching across a gap. FIX: the hard geometric stop is BODY vs BODY (unit squares, reach 0 -- the only thing that physically cannot interpenetrate); contact/engagement stays on the reach-extended box (Stage B, core/contact.py _find_contacts_standoff, unchanged). The body surface sits strictly inside the reach surface (reach>0 always: the P-DEC-1 table is 0.1/0.2/0.3, current flat REACH_SHORT=0.5), so contact fires as cells close through the reach band into body contact -- bodies collide, weapons reach across the closing gap. The stop is symmetric+reach-independent so the reach THROTTLE (_reach_throttle/_effective_reach) is retired from the stop path (both cells cap at the shared body-touch fraction; reach asymmetry -- a longer weapon engaging first -- is expressed by contact firing earlier for the longer-reach box, not a movement handicap). CHARGING preserved/RESTORED: _momentum_speed reads cell_last_speed = the PRE-cap intended step (the charge velocity), so charge shock reflects closing speed; under the old reach-stop, contact never fired so charge shock never triggered at all (verified: head-on now closes to gap 1.0 body-touch and exchanges casualties; a Fast cavalry charge reaches contact and deals more than it takes on the impact tick). Guarded by tests/valoria/test_obb_contact_toi.py (7 tests: contact-fires-at-OBB, head-on no-body-interpenetration+no-stall, cavalry-charge-reaches-contact, grid-path-never-calls-OBB, conservation I1, determinism I2) + test_obb_primitive.py (Stage A, 21 tests, unchanged). I4 GRID ORACLE UNTOUCHED: resolve_toi_and_commit runs only under 'if FIELD_MOVEMENT' (orchestration.py:1405); the FIELD_MOVEMENT=0 byte-exact grid oracle (test_mass_battle_byte_exact.py) is structurally unreachable and stays green. FIELD behaviour changes by design (bodies now close to touch and fight instead of standing off at gap 1.5 doing nothing) -> the bat.py field goldens (cell_field/unit_field, NOT CI-checked per test_mass_battle_byte_exact.py head comment) re-recorded. This MOVES the DG-6-gated 20-row Cannae balance gauge (units that used to freeze at range now engage) -- disclosed, NOT a balance-calibration claim, no balance constant tuned (I5). Plan Stage C + risk R1 amended in spatial_model_v2_plan.md to record the body-stop correction. Departs from the written plan's shared-surface premise -- flagged prominently in the PR body for merge-ratification (CLAUDE.md 2). Stages D (continuous frontage), E (weapon-class reach 0.1/0.2/0.3 + pike troop type), F (historical revalidation + digest re-record), G (retire integer engine) remain.

title: Intent as an offence/defence resolution axis (hold/defend vs press/rout resolve differently)
summary: Jordan directive 2026-07-23: 'a subunit trying to hold ground and defend versus a subunit trying to rout the other resolve differently -- intent makes a big difference in how things resolve.' stance was movement-speed only (STANCE_SPEED_MOD); now it is a signed offence/defence COMMITMENT on the exchange. Anchored to the §A ASYMMETRY (Disciplined Defence +1D Defence, but Standard Advance 'no additional effect') -> DEF=1.0 > OFF=0.5: the doctrine favours the defender, so a holding pin SURVIVES a pressing foe (buys time -- the Cannae centre) instead of cancelling to an even fight, while an aggressor pays for exposure vs a steady wall. summary: Jordan historical research 2026-07-23: 'routs would occur as early as 15% losses with 30% the upper hand.' title: Fractional combat pool — the continuous pool is no longer floored before rolling
summary: Jordan directive 2026-07-23: 'pool must be fractional.' The sigma-boost reads the fractional pool too. So the pool is used at full fractional precision. Wired into resolve_engagements' sigma-head a_net/b_net; the dead-atom net=0 override is preserved. VERIFIED: roll_pool_fractional(3.0) vs 3.7 differ in mean net by ~0.7*0.4 (the fractional die's EV); integer pools reduce exactly to roll_pool; monotone across integer gaps (no quantization plateau).

title: Matched command-granularity honest gauge — fix the envelopment measurement artifact (H3 flagship 0→70.7%)
summary: The honest gauge's composed enveloper/refused presets (_envelop_army = 3 bodies; _refused_army = 2) always faced a SINGLE-subunit opponent built by make_unit. A monolithic subunit is nearly unbreakable by envelopment: the octagon flank/rear multiplier + multi-side shock land on its cells but the casualties DILUTE across its whole HP pool (distribute_casualties), and no section can rout independently, so the per-subunit rout cascade (ED-1019 — a section of the line breaks while a fresh sibling holds) has nothing to bite. title: Envelopment stability diagnosis — H3/H10 side-asymmetry root-caused; moderate-envelopment bands sit in an engine gap (design fork)
summary: Continues ED-MB-0038. Root-caused the ~54pp envelopment side-asymmetry (enveloper ~71% as side A, ~17% as side B; same armies/seeds). NOT an RNG-stream artifact (construction doesn't consume random) and NOT a simple side bias (composed mirrors are side-symmetric ~50-58% @ n=120). It is a DEPLOYMENT-CHAOTIC knife-edge amplified by Lanchester positive feedback: a parity centre (200 troops = 2 cells) is NARROWER than the 3-command enemy (6 cells) → the enemy out-flanks the centre while the wings try to wrap → a two-way race whose tip is decided by integer deployment parity (start-row sweep swings env win-rate 54→50→17→9pp). Side-symmetric avg is ~44% (enveloper slightly LOSES at parity); H3's 70.7 is the favourable side of the chaos. Three regimes measured (envelopment_stability_probe.py vs the 3-command Line): pure-infantry thin centre = chaotic ~44% avg, ~41-54pp swing; deep-narrow centre (width=1,depth=2 — BOTH keys needed, width alone silently ignored) = STABLE (swing 51→7pp) but LOSES (too narrow → bypassed; depth confers no holding without frontage in the frontage-capped attrition model); combined-arms (infantry pin + cavalry orbital-wheel rear, ED-MB-0035) = STABLE + side-symmetric (swing 0-14pp) + decisive (~93-100%), and ~100% vs EVERY defender toughness (deep/disc8/braced/6-command) — the cavalry reaches the unrefaceable rear, nothing moderates it. CONCLUSION: the engine has two envelopment regimes and nothing between; the history-grounded moderate bands H3 55-72 / H4 45-62 are not stably reachable — an engine limitation, not a gauge knob.

title: Cell-primitive damage — fix the aggregate-smear bug (the cell is the primitive); historical Cannae still fails
summary: Jordan directive: 'the cell is the primitive', 'each cell has its own octagon facing', 'each cell has its own capacity to receive and issue damage', 'flank/rear damage is supposed to be cellular', 'damage is supposed to be done to cells'. FOUND THE BUG: _octagon_dmg_mod evaluated each defender cell's own octagon arc then AVERAGED them into one subunit scalar; that scalar multiplied the pair's damage, which distribute_casualties then spread across engaged cells by DENSITY ONLY. So a rear-facing cell and a front-facing cell in the SAME subunit lost identical troops — the 2x rear multiplier merely inflated a uniformly-smeared total, envelopment could not strip a formation shell-inward, and a monolithic subunit was near-unbreakable by envelopment. That is the true upstream cause of BOTH the ED-MB-0038 granularity workaround and the ED-MB-0039 'engine gap'. FIX: _octagon_cell_mods is now the single owner of the per-cell arc (each cell judged on its own facing/local centroid/pin/FOV/reaction clock); _octagon_dmg_mod is redefined as its mean (byte-identical). Gated PC_CELL_DAMAGE allocates each pair's casualties to the defender's contact CELLS weighted by (troops x that cell's own facing multiplier) via distribute_casualties_cellwise (overflow-spilling so cells==hp holds under annihilation); pair TOTAL unchanged, only placement differs. Volley keeps the aggregate spread (area fire has no contact arc). MEASURED: infantry envelopment vs a 3-command line — side-swing 41.0->15.5pp, side-symmetric avg 43.8->57.8% (INTO the history-grounded 55-72 band). So ED-MB-0039's 'moderate envelopment is unreachable / needs a new mechanic' was NOT a missing mechanic: it was this bug. BUT it re-bases the whole battery (gauge 8/20 -> 4/20: C4 93.2->71.2, H11 45.6->15.4, H10 83.3->59.6) because every band was implicitly fitted to the smear — ships GATED OFF, byte-exact verified against the pre-change engine (identical winners + hp to 6dp).

title: The cell is the primitive for MORALE — aggregate-up/modulate-down, per-cell du Picq break-point, contagion; default flipped ON on measurement
summary: Executes Jordan's 2026-07-25 directive ("the cell needs to be the primitive for morale, discipline, quality, stamina, route, health, armour, facing, damage, troops count, etc") for MORALE, the first state to move. Before this the cell was the primitive for GEOMETRY only, so Jordan's own test case ("a cell should be able to have worse morale than another cell in same subunit") was not representable: a rear cell being cut down and a front cell holding shared one scalar. PHASE 1 - cells carry morale; the subunit's morale is the troop-weighted MEAN of its live cells (derived, not stored) and that holistic value pulls its own cells back toward it at a discipline-gated rate (cohere_cells, signed both ways, conserves the aggregate). Erosion scales by FRACTION of the cell, not absolute count, so dense cells are not spuriously braver. PHASE 2 - a broken cell (morale <= 0) stops contributing combat weight while its men REMAIN present and killable (a break is not a casualty event); breaks spread over the 8-neighbourhood lattice, so the spread follows the formation's own shape with no shape-specific code; a body whose broken cells hold CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC of its men is no longer a formation. PHASE 2B - the phase that made phase 2 reachable at all. Phases 1+2 measured BYTE-IDENTICAL to phase 1 across all 20 rows; instrumentation showed 72 of 144 cells 'broken' at exactly -1.0, one uniform write, i.e. cells were breaking as a CONSEQUENCE of the body routing. Root cause was an ASYMMETRY, not a magnitude: bodies get erosion AND a du Picq break-point, cells had erosion only, so a cell had to be destroyed twice over to break by erosion and the body always won that race by construction. check_cell_breaks() gives each cell its own break-point drawn in the same historical 15-30% band, discipline-skewed. FLIP - measured against a same-session flag-OFF control at n=60 in the resolving (multi) mode: win-share 7/20 -> 8/20 and casualty/duration realism 2/20 -> 7/20. The casualty column is the evidence and it is a mechanism producing a SHAPE, not a fitted number: loser losses fall out of 31-40% into 26-30% (H6 79.2 -> 48.9, C7 39.9 -> 32.1), which is du Picq's claim that a body comes apart before it is destroyed. Costs stated: single mode 7/20 -> 5/20 (both flipped rows are sub-1 sigma band-edge moves at n=60 in the mode the gauge documents as non-resolving); C4 91.5 -> 96.7 against a 95 ceiling (~0.5 sigma); reverse-pair symmetry 3.8 -> 3.4 sigma with H4/H11 still ASYMMETRIC and still open. Both byte-exact goldens RE-RECORDED (not pinned off) so the change-detector keeps tracking the shipped engine. UNPLANNED FINDING, recorded not acted on: with per-cell break-points live, PC_STOCHASTIC_ROUT is INERT in the shipped configuration - loser casualties 35.6% with it off vs 36.1% on, no separation. The cells break first and CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC ends the body before the subunit-level draw is consulted. It remains load-bearing on the unseeded fallback path, so it is a retirement CANDIDATE, not dead code. CORRECTION ON THE RECORD: I flagged an 'over-firing' signal (76-100% single-mode draw rates) from the phase-2b run. The flag-OFF control shows those same rows at 100% draws with the flag off - the pre-existing tick-cap artifact the gauge's own docstring documents. I read rows from a run with no control beside it; a number without its control is not a measurement, for a worrying number as much as a flattering one.

title: RETRACTION of the same-day PC_CELL_MORALE flip — the measurement's two arms were not comparable
summary: Supersedes the prior ED-MB-0042 entry's FLIP paragraph. The per-cell morale MECHANISM (phases 1/2/2b) stands and is unchanged; the DEFAULT FLIP and its measurement are withdrawn. CAUSE: between_turn_recovery and reset_morale_between_battles both write the morale SCALAR, which eff_morale stops reading the moment cells are seeded, so under PC_CELL_MORALE they are silent no-ops (verified directly: knock a body's cells to 2.0, call both, still 2.0). The gauge's multi mode runs multi-turn battles and resets morale between them, so the ON arm fought with morale that never recovered while the OFF arm's did. 'The loser breaks earlier' is precisely what an unrecoverable body also produces, so the reported 7->8/20 win-share and 2->7/20 casualty-realism gains cannot be attributed to the mechanism. Reverted: default OFF, _PINNED_OFF back to '0', both byte-exact goldens back to their pre-flip digests, default-pinning test restored with the reason. SAME DEFECT CLASS AS THE erode_morale SILENT NO-OP caught earlier in this same lane and session. That one was fixed as a single instance with no sweep for the pattern, so it recurred and this time reached a shipped default and a golden re-record. The transferable lesson is about the UNIT OF REPAIR: when a defect's cause is 'a representation change orphaned its writers', the repair is every writer, found by grep, not the writer that happened to fail. TWO GENUINE DEFECTS FOUND BY THE FAILING SUITE AND KEPT, both real bugs in the phase-1/2b work and independent of the flip: (1) BORN-BROKEN SUBUNITS — seed_cell_morale ran in Subunit.__post_init__, but a subunit with morale=None inherits from its parent Unit and the _unit back-ref is not set until Unit.__post_init__, strictly later; so an inheriting subunit seeded every cell at eff_morale's no-parent fallback of 0, i.e. born broken, emitting no combat weight and unable to recover because once cells exist eff_morale reads THEM and never falls back to the correct parent scalar. Inheriting subunits are now seeded from Unit.__post_init__. The gauge path passes morale explicitly, which is why the targeted tests and the measurement were green while ten unrelated suite tests were not. (2) A 1-ULP AGGREGATE DEFEATING AN IDENTITY — the troop-weighted mean of N equal values is that value mathematically but not in floats (15 cells at 6.0 -> 5.999999999999999); _morale_sigma divides by morale_start, so a body at full morale reported sigma -1.8e-16 instead of 0, enough to cross a DAMAGE_BY_DEGREE boundary and turn a 6.0 exchange into 0.0. title: Same-side cell exclusion (PC_CELL_EXCLUSION, default ON): inter-subunit deep overlap -48.6%, cross-side -74.4% -- and the deadlock it shipped with
description: Jordan 2026-07-29: 'We need to prevent inter-subunit collisions', with the design steer 'we are using a field system so there shouldn't even be any assignment issues so long as cell boundaries are respected.' resolve_toi_and_commit's own docstring already states the invariant -- 'two unit squares that must never interpenetrate' -- but applied it to CROSS-SIDE pairs only, so a cell of one subunit walked through a cell of another on its own side. This adds the same swept-SAT body-box solve to same-side pairs. No new mechanism, no RNG, no third definition of 'these two bodies touch'. || THE DEFECT IT FIRST SHIPPED WITH, and the more instructive half. It accepted a time-of-impact of s == 0.0, copying the cross-side loop, where that is a safe defensive floor because armies start apart and pre-existing contact is caught upstream by halted_cells. Same-side pairs invert every one of those assumptions: the formation lattice has pitch 1.0 and the bodies are 1.0x1.0, so every adjacent cell in every formation is touching BY CONSTRUCTION and permanently, and no cell is ever halted against its own neighbour. MEASURED: 568,785 of 1,213,199 same-side solves -- 46.9% -- returned exactly 0.0, against 9.84% cross-side. Halted cells FELL 20,356 -> 3,300; resolve calls ROSE 1,482 -> 11,934. Frozen formations never close, never contact, never halt, so every battle ran to the turn cap. That 8.05x TICK inflation was the entire '8.2x slowdown' (47s -> 386s) the pass was blamed for -- which is why a swept-AABB broad phase written to fix the COST bought nothing (386s -> 370s): it culled pairs correctly inside a loop whose ITERATION COUNT was the defect. Broad phase removed; runtime now 1.41x baseline. The rule is s > 0 and introduces no constant: capping at s == 0.0 cannot un-overlap a pre-existing overlap, it freezes the pair where it already sits for zero corrective benefit and total motion cost. || RESULT, on deep overlap (obb_overlap AND penetration depth >= 0.1; the raw boolean is dominated by the lattice's permanent tangency and over-states the defect ~10x): inter-subunit 13,477 -> 6,932 (-48.6%), cross-side 875 -> 224 (-74.4%), same-subunit 43,068 -> 44,531 (+3.4%). NOT zero, for two identified reasons: the rule deliberately skips pairs already overlapping at tick start and nothing in the engine ever separates them (resolve_internal_collisions, ED-MB-0057, is the only primitive built for that and is intra-subunit + grid-era); and the whole solve is gated on toi_deferred = FIELD_MOVEMENT and enemy_cells_float, so formations with no enemy supplied still interpenetrate freely -- same-side exclusion inherits a cross-side precondition it has no reason to. || COST, measured with a control (§0.1 #4): the pass suppresses contact and therefore casualties. Mean end-state hp over all 20 historical rows at t=24 rose 0.8684 -> 0.8939, i.e. total attrition fell 19%, on a casualty model already flagged as far too low. Shipped ON per the standing 'gate models ON' directive with the cost recorded rather than discovered later. || GOLDENS: unit_field 6f594233 -> 0194efcc, cell_field 2a9214eb -> da6d685e. ATTRIBUTION CONTROL: re-running at PC_CELL_EXCLUSION=0 reproduces BOTH previous goldens byte-for-byte, so 100% of the delta is this pass and nothing else in the changeset; both grid modes byte-identical with the flag ON. GUARD: tests/valoria/test_cell_exclusion_no_deadlock.py, mutation-verified -- dropping the s <= 0.0 skip freezes the fixture dead (0 cells moved between tick 1 and tick 6).

description: Corrects ED-MB-0056 and an unpublished intermediate. The field path is continuous; two bodies 0.6 apart round into a collision that never happened. It over-counts. RETRACTED #2, the worse one: '17.31% -> 0.35% with exclusion ON' was measured on an arm where the exclusion pass had DEADLOCKED the engine (ED-MB-0059) -- cells were not overlapping because they were not moving. It reports body-box interpenetration via geometry.obb_overlap -- the engine's existing single owner of 'these two bodies overlap', not a fourth definition -- THRESHOLDED BY PENETRATION DEPTH. Depth is load-bearing: the lattice pitch is 1.0 and the bodies are 1.0x1.0, so _sat_separated's documented boundary (centre distance exactly 1.0 counts as separated) means neighbours sit EXACTLY ON the predicate's boundary by construction and any sub-millimetre jitter flips it. description: CORRECTION ROW (append-only; supersedes the earlier ED-MB-0063 row on three points). An independent read-only critic pass ran against the committed claims and refuted part of them. The headline finding -- F2 is a confounded TEST, not an engine regression -- SURVIVES and was independently re-derived. Three things were wrong and are corrected here rather than quietly edited, because the errors are more instructive than the result. (1) THE STATED CAUSE WAS WRONG. The earlier row said the pool moved 3.6 -> 1.333 because 'different cells carry different troops'. FALSE: Subunit.distribution defaults to 'uniform', so every cell holds troop_count/len(ids) and ranks 0 and 2 are identical in troops. The real mechanism is SUPPORT DEPTH, in core/exchange.py::_pair_engaged_troops: front_r = min(r) over the contact cells, and deeper cells are credited at SUPPORT_WEIGHTS {1:1.0, 2:0.7, 3:0.5}. Contacting rank 0 leaves two ranks behind it -> (5 + 5*1.0 + 5*0.7)/15 = 0.9 of base; contacting rank 2 leaves none -> 5/15 = 1/3. At base pool 4 that reproduces 3.6 and 1.3333 to the digit. (2) THE 'REFUTED' HYPOTHESIS WAS CORRECT IN CONCEPT AND DISMISSED ON THE WRONG FUNCTION. The earlier row recorded support-stack loss as refuted by measuring geometry.support_engage_frac at 1.0 in both arms. That function is NEVER CALLED on this path -- orchestration.py guards it with `if POOL_VARIANT != "C-ii"` and POOL_VARIANT == 'C-ii' -- and its min(1.0, ...) cap would have hidden the asymmetry regardless. So the right idea was discarded by pattern-matching a NAME instead of following the live path, and a wrong idea was adopted in its place. Both the failed refutation and the retro-fitted explanation passed my own adversarial pass and were caught only by a structurally independent reader; that is the argument for the relay, not a footnote to it. (3) THE FALSIFIER WAS OVERSTATED: 2/3, NOT 3/3. OCTAGON_DMG_MULT['YELLOW'] has NO readers anywhere -- the only live read is ['RED'] (orchestration.py:1316) and the flank value is INTERPOLATED (mult = 1 - arc*(RED-1)/2), never looked up. Re-run cleanly with a count assertion: the YELLOW 1.5 -> 1.0 mutant kills NOTHING (6/6 pass). The earlier '3/3 mutants killed' was wrong, and a wrong falsifier is worse than none, because 0.1 #3 makes the artifact the evidence. RED 2.0 -> 1.0 (kills 3) and RED 2.0 -> 2.5 (kills 2) stand. Side finding, worth its own look: the YELLOW constant is dead config. (4) PRIOR ART NOT CREDITED. audit/2026-07-30-mb-session-retrospective/00_lessons.md had ALREADY classified F2 as a test-premise defect and named orig-frame support depth. The earlier row presented the diagnosis as fresh. It is an implementation of that classification, not a discovery -- and the correct mechanism was sitting 14 lines below the bisect table that was quoted from the same document. STRONGER FALSIFIER ADDED (critic finding D). '7 of 12 seeds gave exactly 2.0x' is near-vacuous: once the body is held fixed both arms share one RNG stream and the ratio is arithmetically forced. The new test_arc_ratio_is_invariant_to_the_fractional_pool_flag parametrizes PC_FRACTIONAL_POOL over both settings, which is the property that was FALSE before (ON failed, OFF passed -- the flag-dependence that DEFINED F2). Mutation-verified by reintroducing the def_adv +/-1 confound: it fails on [1] and passes on [0], reproducing F2's exact signature. The fixture now also pins PC_FRACTIONAL_POOL explicitly instead of inheriting the ambient default. RECORDED, NOT FIXED (critic findings A/B/C, all pre-existing): A -- test_rear_penalty_persists_across_reaction_window does NOT traverse the window it names. The reaction counter is consecutive-tick in a per-subunit map, _arc_pair builds a FRESH Subunit per call, so _cnt can never exceed 1 while FACING_REACTION_TICKS is 2; the wheel branch is unreachable and an engine that DID wheel would still pass. Varying t varies the tick LABEL, not elapsed time. The correct form ticks a persistent subunit, as test_visible_flank_refuses_after_delay already does in the same file. Noted in the docstring so routing it through _arc_pair does not imply a validation that did not happen. B -- test_front_takes_no_arc_penalty still uses the def_adv +/-1 pairing. Justifying that as 'an inequality that survives the confound' is a structural claim with no control, which is the shape this entry exists to condemn. Left in place, flagged. C -- the isolation is scenario-dependent, not structural: cell_facing_vec also feeds _per_cell_angle_mod (charge-shock, envelopment-shock, brace-recoil) and _compute_atom_sides, inert only because this fixture has no brace, no momentum differential, one subunit per side. Stated in the docstring so the precondition is not silently inherited -- which is exactly how the original confound was inherited. The two are not reconciled and should not be read as the same measurement.
